label: I
name: F=MA
tagline: Algebra- and calculus-based mechanics: everything you need to walk into the qualifying exam knowing the tricks, not just the topic names

sections.title: Toolkit: Before You Start
sections.blurb: Not tested on its own, but every later unit quietly assumes it.

modules.title: Units, Dimensional Analysis & Estimation
modules.description: Checking an answer by its units, order-of-magnitude sanity checks, and the Fermi-style estimation questions that open some exams.

modules.title: Vectors: Components, Dot & Cross Products
modules.description: Breaking vectors into components, and what the two products actually mean physically rather than just how to compute them.

modules.title: Calculus for Physics I: Derivatives
modules.description: Reading velocity and acceleration as derivatives, and the handful of rules every kinematics problem quietly assumes.

modules.title: Calculus for Physics II: Integrals
modules.description: Going from acceleration back to velocity and position, and treating an integral as a literal area under a curve.

modules.title: Approximations & Small-Angle Expansions
modules.description: Taylor series, sin θ ≈ θ, and the binomial approximation: one shortcut that shows up in half of all oscillation and orbit problems.

modules.title: Problem-Solving Strategy
modules.description: How to set a problem up before touching an equation: choosing axes, isolating the system, and checking limiting cases.

modules.title: Data Analysis: Graphs & Uncertainty
modules.description: Pulling a relationship out of a data table, straightening a curved graph, and what error bars are telling you.

sections.title: Kinematics
sections.blurb: Describing motion before worrying about what causes it.

modules.title: Motion in One Dimension
modules.description: Position, velocity and acceleration as a chain of derivatives, plus the constant-acceleration equations everyone memorizes.

modules.title: Motion Graphs
modules.description: Reading and sketching x-t, v-t and a-t graphs, and pulling displacement out of areas and slopes.

modules.title: Free Fall & Variable Acceleration
modules.description: Constant-g problems, fall with drag, and how to set things up when the acceleration refuses to stay constant.

modules.title: Two-Dimensional & Projectile Motion
modules.description: Independent x and y motion, range and max-height optimization, and projectiles landing on slopes.

modules.title: Relative Motion
modules.description: Switching reference frames, river-crossing and pursuit problems, and drawing relative-velocity diagrams that actually help.

sections.title: Newton's Laws & Forces
sections.blurb: What makes things accelerate, and how to account for every push and pull.

modules.title: Newton's Three Laws & Free Body Diagrams
modules.description: Finding every force systematically, and the discipline of drawing one clean diagram per object before writing a single equation.

modules.title: Friction
modules.description: Static against kinetic friction, the friction cone, and multi-block systems where the block you would guess moves first is the wrong one.

modules.title: Tension, Pulleys & Connected Systems
modules.description: Massless string and pulley idealizations, Atwood machines, and writing the constraint that ties two objects together.

modules.title: Springs & Hooke's Law
modules.description: Spring forces in series and parallel, and setting up the equation of motion for spring-connected blocks.

modules.title: Circular Motion
modules.description: Centripetal force, vertical circles, and the minimum-speed-at-the-top condition that trips up almost everyone once.

modules.title: Banked Curves & Conical Pendulums
modules.description: Combining gravity and the normal force on a tilted circular path, with no friction to lean on.

modules.title: Gravitation & Orbits
modules.description: Newton's law of gravitation, orbital speed and period, and escape velocity.

modules.title: Kepler's Laws
modules.description: Elliptical orbits, the equal-area law, and how period relates to radius for planets and satellites.

sections.title: Work, Energy & Momentum
sections.blurb: Two conservation laws that answer questions forces alone make painful.

modules.title: Work & the Work-Energy Theorem
modules.description: Computing work along a path, including curved ones, and connecting it straight to the change in kinetic energy.

modules.title: Conservative Forces & Potential Energy
modules.description: Gravitational and spring potential energy, and reading force directly off a potential energy curve.

modules.title: Conservation of Energy
modules.description: Setting up energy equations for multi-stage systems without re-deriving the kinematics at every stage.

modules.title: Power
modules.description: Instantaneous against average power, and problems where the power, not the force, is what is limited.

modules.title: Momentum & Impulse
modules.description: The impulse-momentum theorem, and impacts where the force is not constant.

modules.title: Collisions in One and Two Dimensions
modules.description: Elastic and inelastic collisions, and conserving momentum as a vector when things do not hit head-on.

modules.title: Center of Mass & Systems of Particles
modules.description: Locating the center of mass, and treating a complicated multi-body system as one effective particle.

sections.title: Rotational Motion
sections.blurb: Everything from the last two units, rewritten for things that spin.

modules.title: Angular Kinematics
modules.description: Angular position, velocity and acceleration, and how each one maps back to its straight-line counterpart.

modules.title: Torque & Static Equilibrium
modules.description: Torque about a pivot, and solving for unknown forces on rigid bodies that are not moving at all.

modules.title: Moment of Inertia
modules.description: Computing and combining moments of inertia, including the parallel axis theorem, without memorizing every shape.

modules.title: Rotational Dynamics: τ = Iα
modules.description: Newton's second law for rotation, applied to pulleys with real mass and to rotating rigid bodies.

modules.title: Angular Momentum
modules.description: Conserving angular momentum in collisions, in closing orbits, and in systems that change shape mid-problem.

modules.title: Rolling Without Slipping
modules.description: The rolling constraint, translation and rotation together, and who wins a race down an incline.

sections.title: Oscillations
sections.blurb: Systems that get pushed back toward where they started.

modules.title: Simple Harmonic Motion
modules.description: Spring-block systems, the SHM differential equation, and how amplitude, phase and frequency relate.

modules.title: Pendulums
modules.description: Simple and physical pendulums, and where the small-angle period formula actually comes from.

modules.title: Energy in Oscillators
modules.description: Following kinetic and potential energy trading places through a full cycle.

modules.title: Effective Potentials & Equilibrium
modules.description: Finding equilibrium points and the oscillation frequency from any potential energy function, with a live oscillator to test it on.

sections.title: Fluids & Extra Mechanics
sections.blurb: The two mechanics topics that do not fit anywhere else.

modules.title: Pressure & Buoyancy
modules.description: Hydrostatic pressure, Archimedes' principle, and floating, sinking and partly-submerged objects.

modules.title: Non-Inertial Frames & Pseudo-Forces
modules.description: Solving a problem from inside an accelerating or rotating frame instead of fighting it from outside.

label: II
name: USAPhO
tagline: Free-response mastery across the full syllabus, at the depth the actual exam expects

sections.title: Electrostatics
sections.blurb: Charges at rest, and the two tools that make them tractable.

modules.title: Coulomb's Law & Superposition
modules.description: Forces between point charges, and adding up the field from a handful of charges by hand.

modules.title: Continuous Charge Distributions
modules.description: Setting up, and actually finishing, the integrals for the field of rods, rings, disks and shells.

modules.title: Gauss's Law
modules.description: Choosing a symmetric surface that turns a nasty integral into one line of algebra.

modules.title: Electric Potential
modules.description: Potential from point and continuous charges, and how field and potential are two views of the same thing.

modules.title: Conductors & Capacitance
modules.description: How charge rearranges itself on a conductor, and parallel-plate and spherical capacitor problems.

modules.title: Dielectrics & Field Energy
modules.description: Capacitors with a dielectric inside, and where the energy in an electric field is actually stored.

sections.title: Circuits
sections.blurb: Getting current and voltage out of a network without guessing.

modules.title: Current, Resistance & Ohm's Law
modules.description: Current density, resistivity, and reducing basic series and parallel networks.

modules.title: Kirchhoff's Laws
modules.description: The loop and junction rules for multi-loop circuits, and a systematic way to reduce them.

modules.title: RC Circuits & Transients
modules.description: Charging and discharging capacitors, and reasoning with the time constant instead of re-solving the differential equation.

modules.title: Tricky Networks
modules.description: Wheatstone bridges, infinite ladders, and symmetry arguments that skip the algebra entirely.

sections.title: Magnetism & Induction
sections.blurb: Moving charge makes fields, and changing fields push charge back.

modules.title: Magnetic Force
modules.description: Force on moving charges and on current-carrying wires, and circular motion inside a magnetic field.

modules.title: Biot-Savart Law
modules.description: Computing a magnetic field directly from the current that makes it.

modules.title: Ampere's Law
modules.description: Using symmetry to get the field of wires, solenoids and toroids without touching Biot-Savart.

modules.title: Faraday's Law & Lenz's Law
modules.description: EMF from changing flux, and a reliable way to get the induced current's direction right every time.

modules.title: Motional EMF
modules.description: Conductors moving through magnetic fields, and the force balance in generator and rail problems.

modules.title: Inductance & LR/LC Circuits
modules.description: Self-inductance, energy stored in an inductor, and circuits that oscillate on their own.

sections.title: Thermodynamics
sections.blurb: Heat, work and the bookkeeping that connects them.

modules.title: Temperature & the First Law
modules.description: Heat, work and internal energy, kept straight without sign-convention mistakes.

modules.title: Kinetic Theory of Gases
modules.description: Deriving pressure from molecules hitting a wall, and what temperature really measures.

modules.title: Ideal Gas Law & Equipartition
modules.description: The ideal gas law rebuilt from first principles, and counting degrees of freedom correctly.

modules.title: Heat Engines & the Second Law
modules.description: Efficiency limits, the Carnot cycle, and why perpetual motion machines fail.

modules.title: Entropy
modules.description: Entropy change in reversible and irreversible processes, used as a shortcut and not just a definition.

modules.title: PV Diagrams & Real Cycles
modules.description: Reading a multi-step cycle and computing work and heat one leg at a time.

sections.title: Waves & Sound
sections.blurb: Disturbances that carry energy without carrying matter.

modules.title: Wave Basics
modules.description: Wave speed, wavelength and frequency, and the wave equation on a string.

modules.title: Superposition & Standing Waves
modules.description: Waves adding together, and the standing-wave modes on strings and in pipes.

modules.title: Beats & Interference
modules.description: Beat frequency, and interference patterns from more than one source.

modules.title: The Doppler Effect
modules.description: Frequency shifts for moving sources, moving observers and reflecting surfaces.

sections.title: Optics
sections.blurb: Light as rays when it can be, as waves when it must be.

modules.title: Reflection & Refraction
modules.description: Snell's law, total internal reflection, and the basics of how an image forms.

modules.title: Thin Lenses & Mirrors
modules.description: The lens and mirror equation, ray diagrams, and chaining several optical elements together.

modules.title: Diffraction & Interference
modules.description: Double-slit interference and diffraction gratings, including where the bright fringes actually land.

modules.title: Thin-Film Interference
modules.description: Phase shifts on reflection and the colour patterns they produce in thin films.

sections.title: Modern Physics
sections.blurb: Where classical physics stops giving the right answer.

modules.title: Special Relativity: Kinematics
modules.description: Time dilation, length contraction and simultaneity, without the usual paradox confusion.

modules.title: Relativistic Energy & Momentum
modules.description: Mass-energy equivalence, and collisions at speeds where Newton no longer applies.

modules.title: The Photoelectric Effect
modules.description: Photon energy, work function, and reading a stopping-potential graph.

modules.title: The Bohr Model
modules.description: Quantized energy levels, and the emission and absorption spectra they produce.

modules.title: de Broglie Waves
modules.description: Matter waves and wave-particle duality, and when each picture is the useful one.

sections.title: Nuclear & Particle Physics
sections.blurb: Inside the nucleus, and the particles below it.

modules.title: Radioactivity & Nuclear Decay
modules.description: Half-life, decay chains, alpha, beta and gamma decay, and activity against time.

modules.title: Nuclear Binding Energy & Reactions
modules.description: Mass defect, binding energy per nucleon, and the energy released in fission and fusion.

modules.title: Intro to Particle Physics
modules.description: The fundamental particles, and the conservation laws that decide which interactions are allowed.

sections.title: Data Analysis & Advanced Techniques
sections.blurb: The techniques that separate a good score from a medal.

modules.title: Data Analysis & Uncertainty
modules.description: Propagating experimental uncertainty, straightening data, and the graph-reading problems on real free-response exams.

modules.title: Lagrangian Mechanics: An Alternative Approach
modules.description: Setting up and using the Euler-Lagrange equation as a faster route through constrained multi-body problems.

modules.title: Coupled Oscillators & Normal Modes
modules.description: Two or more masses joined by springs, and finding the normal-mode frequencies without brute force.

modules.title: Boundary-Value Problems in E&M
modules.description: The method of images and other symmetry tricks for field problems Gauss's law alone cannot solve.

modules.title: Four-Vectors & Relativistic Doppler
modules.description: The four-vector formalism as a cleaner way to handle relativistic collisions, plus the relativistic Doppler shift.
